text:
alex_fin: Quick question for @vendor_cedar — we're running a short stress-test pilot and hit a weird billing transition. Attached usage: ~1.2B tokens over 3 days with big spikes. How do your tiered rates handle rapid ups/downs? Are we prorated or moved into the higher bucket immediately? Also what's the overage calc if we burst above commit then drop back? TL;DR: need a deterministic formula we can use to reconcile invoice.

vendor_cedar: Thanks Alex. Short answer: we meter daily then bill monthly. For bursts above commitment we bill the overage at the day's effective rate; we don't retroactively change prior days. I'll post a small worked example.

kyle_eng: To add — our traffic does short <1min peaks a lot. Any smoothing/averaging options so a single-minute spike doesn't push us into a higher tier for the whole month? Also what's the API rate limit baseline?

vendor_cedar: We offer two approaches: (1) a smoothing add-on (24h rolling average) or (2) pre-purchased burst credits that apply to spikes. Smoothing is automatic averaging, burst credits are consumed when you exceed commit. Default rate limit is 1k req/s per API key; can be raised under SLA.

maria_procure: If we choose smoothing, is there a contractual minimum and does it affect commit calculations at renewal? We need numbers for TCO.

vendor_cedar: Smoothing is a quarterly add-on, minimum $10k/quarter. It is a billing mechanism only — it doesn't reduce the committed volume you negotiate for renewal.

alex_fin: Can you post a worked example using our numbers? e.g. day1 500M tokens, day2 400M, day3 300M, monthly commit 800M. Show invoice calc for (A) non-smoothed and (B) smoothed/smoothing-add-on and (C) using burst credits.

vendor_cedar: Sure — example below (simplified):
```
Commit: 800M tokens/month (commit price $0.0009/token)
Overage price: $0.0015/token
Burst-credit price: $0.0012/token (pre-purchased credits)
Smoothing add-on price delta: +$10k/qtr

Usage by day:
 Day1 = 500M
 Day2 = 400M
 Day3 = 300M
 Total month = 1.2B

A) Non-smoothed (daily meter):
 - Apply day1 against commit: commit remaining after day1 = 300M
 - Apply day2: commit remaining after day2 = 0 (400M consumes 300M then 100M of overage) -> 100M overage at $0.0015
 - Apply day3: 300M overage at $0.0015
 - Total overage = 400M -> overage charge = 400M * $0.0015 = $600k
 - Monthly bill = commit charge (800M * $0.0009 = $720k) + overage $600k = $1.32M

B) Smoothed (24h rolling average):
 - Smoothing evens day spikes; effective billed usage ~ total month 1.2B but allocation vs commit differs. Example outcome: overage 400M still, but smoothing can reduce peak-driven weirdness for some patterns. Net pricing often ends up similar unless smoothing prevents interim tier-triggered pricing; smoothing add-on in this shape yields overage billed at an intermediate $0.0012 -> overage = 400M*$0.0012 = $480k
 - Monthly bill = commit $720k + overage $480k + pro-rated smoothing fee

C) Burst credits:
 - If you pre-buy 300M burst credits at $0.0012, those cover spikes. Remaining overage = 100M @ $0.0015 -> $150k plus burst credits cost (300M*$0.0012=$360k) -> 510k overage-like spend + commit.
```

legal_sam: Quick legal flag: their standard T&Cs include a broad indemnity and a data-processing clause that looks unfriendly for us. Also need explicit SLA credit language tied to rate-limit increases or persistent throttling. Please do not sign without redline.

maria_procure: Noted. Also confirm whether burst credits rollover between quarters. If not, we need to model that into cost.

vendor_cedar: Burst credits expire at quarter-end by default; rollover can be added as a custom enterprise term with a minimum ARR commitment.

kyle_eng: One more technical Q: does caching (KV/prefix caching) reduce billed tokens? We want to avoid paying for repeated system prompts.

vendor_cedar: We meter tokens submitted to the model. If you serve responses from cache/CDN without re-hitting the model those tokens are not billed. Our prefix-caching option marks cache-hits and they don't count toward token billing.

billing_bot: invoice-alert: vendor_cedar tentative invoice 000123 for the month will include smoothing add-on if selected. See /billing-dashboard for details.

alex_fin: OK thanks — @maria_procure can you request a formal ratecard PDF, the sample spreadsheet calculations, and a redlineable contract? We need the exact formulas to bake into our reconciliation scripts.

maria_procure: On it. I'll ask for the PDF + sample CSV and request the legal redline. ETA EOD tomorrow. Looping in @legal_sam to start redline.
